column1: *** THREE LUWINSKI MEN, FIFTEEN YEARS, WITH TRADES AND ADDRESSES ***
column2: a phrase search for LUWINSKI across the whole post-war run returns TEN pages in eight volumes: Namenteil 1957, 1959, 1961, 1963, 1964, 1967 and 1970, and the 1970-71 telephone book. Every one of the three men is already in the family tree and every one of them is dead, so all three are named here.

column1: MANFRED — and the trade matches the emigration roll exactly
column2: LUWINSKI MANFRED SCHLOSSER TGL EGELLSSTR 16 in 1957, 1959 and 1961 · "LUWINSKI MANFR MODSCHLOSS" in the 1963 street section · "—MANFRED MODELLSCHLOSSER -27 EGELLSSTR NR 16" in 1964 · "—MANFRED MODELLS[CHLOSSER]" in 1967 · and again in the 1970 street section. TEGEL, EGELLSSTRASSE 16, FOR AT LEAST THIRTEEN YEARS.

column1: and why that is him and not a namesake
column2: the 1965 ICEM nominal roll already read by this archive gives MANFRED LUWINSKI, MODEL FITTER, Berlin to Melbourne, care of MR H. MARQUARDT. *** MODELLSCHLOSSER IS MODEL FITTER. *** The tree has him as MANFRED JOACHIM LUWINSKI, born 14 November 1933, died at Brisbane 20 September 2012 — and it also holds HELGA ERNA MARQUARDT WAGNER née LUWINSKI, born 1934, which is where the Marquardt on the roll comes from. Three sources, one man.

column1: and one oddity recorded rather than explained
column2: HE IS STILL IN THE 1970 VOLUME, five years after the roll has him flying to Australia. A directory lag, a household left behind, or a return — nothing read here says which.

column1: JOACHIM — a trade nobody had
column2: LUWINSKI JOACHIM OFENSETZER 65 RAMLER-STR 15 in 1967, and "LUWINSKI JOACHIM OFEN-SETZER" in the 1970 street section. AN OFENSETZER IS A STOVE-FITTER. WEDDING, RAMLERSTRASSE 15. The tree has JOACHIM LUWINSKI, born 30 November 1940, died 30 December 2006 — Manfred's younger brother — with no occupation and no address of any kind.

column1: KURT — the other Kurt, and he had a telephone
column2: LUWINSKI KURT POSTFACHARB -21 STEPHANSTR 7 in 1964 · "- KURT POSTFARB 41 PETER-VISCHER-25" in 1967 · "LUWINSKI KURT POSTFARB" in the 1970 street section · and in the 1970-71 telephone book, "LUWINSKI KURT 4 12 25 12 · BEAMTER · 52 WALDSTR. 60". A post-office worker who by 1970 is a Beamter, a civil servant, with a line of his own.

column1: *** AND HE IS NOT DERRICK'S FATHER, WHICH NEEDS SAYING ***
column2: KURT ISRAEL LUWINSKI LEFT GERMANY IN 1933 AND DIED IN JOHANNESBURG ON 15 DECEMBER 1968 — corrected here 22 September; this line carried 1969, the superseded family-tree date, against the archive's own correction from the Johannesburg Chevrah Kadisha burial register. He cannot be in a 1970 Berlin telephone book. The tree holds a second Kurt Luwinski — the son of LEO LUWINSKI (b. 1902) and MARTHA FUHL, recorded as dying in 1995 with no birth date, no place and no occupation. THE BERLIN POSTAL WORKER FITS HIM AND IS NOT PROVED TO BE HIM: the link is a surname, a city and an era, which is a correspondence and not an identification. Recorded as a candidate.

column1: the spelling sweep that came with it
column2: LUWINSKY returns NOTHING in the whole post-war run. LOWINSKI returns thirty-five pages across twenty-one volumes — a separate and much commoner Berlin surname, and the reason the pre-war full-text search fuzzes LU into LO. The two must not be merged.

column1: # ——— AND THE OTHER HALF OF THE SWEEP: ROW 179, AUGUSTE UNDER HER LAST SURNAME ———
*** "FRICKE AUGUSTE" ACROSS FORTY POST-WAR VOLUMES RETURNS THREE PAGES, AND THEY ARE TWO WOMEN ***
column2: 1957 Namenteil page 518: "FRICKE AUGUSTE RENTN CHLB 1 KAIS-FRIEDR-STR 79" — a PENSIONER at Kaiser-Friedrich-Straße 79, Charlottenburg. 1963 street section page 850 and 1970 street section page 287: "FRICKE AUGUSTE PUTZFRAU" and "FRICKE AUGUSTE", the same building both years, among Fröhlich, Kaldenbach, Luckow and Stinka. A PUTZFRAU IS A CLEANER, AND A WORKING CLEANER IN 1963 IS NOT A SEVENTY-YEAR-OLD PENSIONER OF 1957. Two different women.

column1: so the candidate appears in exactly one year
column2: the 1957 Charlottenburg pensioner is in NO OTHER VOLUME OF THE RUN, and in NO BERLIN TELEPHONE BOOK 1969-1980. Four Fricke blocks in the Namenteil were opened directly — 1952, 1954, 1963 and 1970 — and none of them holds an Auguste under her own name or on the dash.

column1: what that shape means, IF the 1957 woman is Lizzy
column2: she was in Berlin in 1957 and gone by 1959. *** AND SHE WAS STILL IN BERLIN TWO YEARS AFTER HER MOTHER DIED. *** JOHANNA THIMM DIED AT ZEUTERN ON 30 OCTOBER 1955. So Lizzy did not go to Baden to nurse her mother — she went afterwards, and she died at Kraichtal, the same town, on 22 June 1975.

column1: and the bound, which is the whole of it
column2: THE IDENTIFICATION IS STILL UNPROVED AND THIS CHANGES NOTHING ABOUT THAT. One entry, one year, a common forename and a common surname, and no age, no birth date and no maiden name on the line. What the sweep does is turn "there is a candidate in 1957" into "there is a candidate in 1957 AND IN NO OTHER YEAR", which is a different and more useful statement. The 1975 death registration at Kraichtal remains the document that would settle it.

column1: the dash convention, and why this sweep is not exhaustive
column2: in the Namenteil only the first entry of a surname run is spelt out; the rest hang off a dash. A phrase search for "Fricke Auguste" therefore cannot find a dashed "—Auguste". The four blocks opened by hand were checked for dashed Augustes and had none, but twenty-three volumes were not opened. STATED AS A BOUND, NOT GLOSSED OVER.

column1: # *** AND THE SAME SWEEP RUN ON LEIBHOLZ — WHICH IS THE SURVIVORS' SIDE OF THE STORY ***
# The pre-war volumes track this surname DISAPPEARING: seventeen householders in 1938, six in 1942,
# and every name carrying "Israel" gone. Nobody here had ever asked the opposite question — WHO WAS
# STILL THERE AFTERWARDS. LEIBHOLZ returns NINETEEN pages across seventeen post-war volumes.
# Telephone numbers are deliberately not transcribed below. They add nothing and some of these
# people may have living children.
*** AGNES — AND SHE IS HEINRICH'S WIDOW ***
column2: 1957 Namenteil: "LEIBHOLZ AGNES RENTN SW 61 MEHRINGDAMM 109". 1959: the same line. AND SHE IS STILL AT THE SAME ADDRESS IN THE 1975-76 TELEPHONE BOOK, "Leibholz Agnes · 61 Mehringdamm 109" — NINETEEN YEARS AT ONE ADDRESS, and a line of her own by the end.

column1: and the loop that closes
column2: HEINRICH LEIBHOLZ, born 16.10.1890, is this archive's CONTROL CASE — the man who proved that vanishing from the Berlin directory after 1942 does not mean death, because he died on 9 AUGUST 1948. Mapping the Lives gives his wife as AGNES née KERGER, born 10.03.1889. And SOPHIE LEIBHOLZ, filling in a relief questionnaire IN SHANGHAI IN 1946, named him with "wife AGNES" and asked where he was. HE HAD SURVIVED, HE DIED TWO YEARS LATER, AND HIS WIDOW LIVED ON AT MEHRINGDAMM FOR ANOTHER QUARTER-CENTURY.

column1: ELLA, a nurse, and two addresses
column2: 1957 and 1959: "—ELLA KRANKENSCHWESTER SCHBG DOMINICUSSTR 43". 1964 and 1967: "—ELLA KRKSCHWEST 62 WILLMANNDAMM 3", and the 1963 and 1970 street sections carry her there too. A hospital nurse, in Schöneberg for at least thirteen years. THE 1938 DIRECTORY HAS "Ella (Krankenschwester, Schöneberg, Reppichstr 28)" — the same trade and the same district, twenty-six years earlier. Almost certainly one woman across the war, and NOT ASSERTED as one.

column1: and the street is worth a note and no more
column2: WILLMANNDAMM 3. This archive has recorded for a week that one of the two located Leibholz STOLPERSTEINE is at WILLMANNDAMM 6. Three doors apart, and that is all it is. Nothing read here connects them.

column1: CHARLOTTE
column2: 1957 through 1967 at "NEUK HASENHEIDE 61-62", and in the 1963 and 1970 street sections at what reads as a different building. No trade given in any year.

column1: GERHARD, Dr
column2: 1957, 1959 and 1961: "—GERHARD DR DIPLVOLKSWIRT STGL ALBRECHTSTR 73a" — a doctor of economics in Steglitz. *** NOT Dr Uri Gerhard Leibholz, the constitutional lawyer born 15.11.1901, who died at Göttingen in 1982 and appears in the 1939 census at Herzberger Landstraße there. Two different men and the surname is rare enough that somebody will eventually merge them. ***

column1: FELIX, and then HILDE at the same address
column2: 1969-70 telephone book: "Leibholz Felix · 33 Wiesbadener Str. 57". 1975-76: "Leibholz Hilde · 33 Wiesbadener Str. 57" — THE SAME FLAT, and Felix gone from it. A widow succeeding a husband is the obvious reading and it is only a reading. THE 1938-1940 DIRECTORIES HAVE "FELIX, PENSIONÄR, NW40 SCHARNHORSTSTR 25" and the 1939 census has LEIBHOLZ, FELIX, born 19.06.1877, with MARTHA née RIEDE, at that address. A Felix born 1877 would be ninety-two in 1969. POSSIBLE AND NOT LIKELY; a son or a namesake is the better guess and neither is evidenced.

column1: ERNA
column2: 1980-81 telephone book, "Leibholz Erna · 20 Streitstr. 39" — Spandau. The last Leibholz in the run.

column1: *** AND ONE ABSENCE THAT WAS LOOKED FOR ON PURPOSE ***
column2: FRIDA LEIBBHOLZ née SPREE, Samuel's non-Jewish widow, born Berlin 12 May 1888 and with no death date in the 1939 census database, IS IN NONE OF THE FORTY VOLUMES. Neither is any Frida Leibholz. The doubled-B spelling returns nothing at all in the post-war run, which is expected — it was one clerk's slip on one census card, not a form of the name. WHERE SHE WENT IS NOT ANSWERED HERE.

column1: the shape of the whole thing
column2: SEVENTEEN LEIBHOLZ HOUSEHOLDERS IN BERLIN IN 1938. SIX IN 1942. AND IN THE POST-WAR BOOKS, SIX NAMES ACROSS THIRTY YEARS — Agnes, Ella, Charlotte, Gerhard, Felix and Hilde, then Erna alone in 1980. Not one of them is documented as belonging to the Schubin family, and that is the point: THE SURVIVORS OF THIS SURNAME IN BERLIN ARE THE OTHER LEIBHOLZ FAMILIES. Kurt's people were in Johannesburg, Potsdam and a grave at Auschwitz.
